# v13.2 cannot be deployed: pages pins one engine version and devindex has no home

## Context

@tobiu, asked directly what is missing for the next release, 2026-09-21:

> *"the big problem is that we always deploy releases ⇒ neomjs/pages repo. so far, this uses neo (the engine) as a dependency, runs build-all on it, and deploys dev mode and dist versions. now, neomjs/devindex would get lost if we just deploy the next release as is. … in theory we could delay these items directly after the release and before the deployment, but i am sure that you get my point."*

**The point being that a release you cannot deploy is not cut.** Deferring the topology to the gap between "release" and "deployment" surfaces it at the moment of maximum pressure and minimum design time.

**Milestone #9 is 104 closed / 7 open and contains no deployment item.** The release reads 94 % done while the blocker is unrepresented. That is why this is an issue on the milestone rather than a comment somewhere: a release requirement needs an owner, acceptance criteria, and a place a release plan looks.

## The Problem

**`neomjs/pages` pins exactly one engine version, and that pin is the coupling:**

```json
// neomjs/pages/package.json — measured 2026-09-21
"dependencies": { "neo.mjs": "13.1.0" }
```

One dependency, an `update-neo-version` script, and **no `.github/workflows` directory**. Everything it publishes is built against that single pin.

So a repository with its own release cadence has no third option. **`neomjs/devindex`** — active, pushed the same day — is either rebuilt against whatever the engine pins, coupling its releases to ours, or it is not in the deployment at all. "Gets lost" is the accurate description of the current pipeline's behaviour, not an exaggeration.

**This is pre-split infrastructure.** `ROADMAP.md` line 17 already states *"v13.2 is the first org-spanning release"* and names four repos, while the deployment pipeline still models one.

## The Architectural Reality

**Prior art exists and works.** `neomjs/pages2` is a live Pages site (`neomjs.github.io/pages2`) serving four independent neo workspaces pinned from `^2.3.2` to `^9.13.1`; its last demo landed 2025-06-13. It never stopped — it is working proof that independently pinned workspaces coexist on one Pages site. *(Corrected 2026-09-22: this paragraph first called it cold and asked why it stopped.)*

**`learn/` is now three trees, and two of them are one taxonomy by construction:**

```
engine   learn/benefits/   ArchitectureOverview.md  Introduction.md  body/
brain    learn/benefits/                                             brain/
devindex learn/            Backend  EthicalManifesto  FAQ  Introduction  Methodology  OptIn  OptOut  UserGuide
```

`benefits/body` and `benefits/brain` are named after ADR 0018's two hemispheres, and the decision records are one series split across both repositories: the engine holds 12 ADRs and the Brain 28, with no shared number, together exactly 0001–0040. `learn/agentos/` exists in **both** engine and brain with **disjoint files** (engine: `AGENTS_ATLAS`, `CoreSkills`, `NeuralLink`…; brain: `A2A`, `AiConfigModel`, `CodeExecution`…), so a union is **additive, not colliding**: the 148 engine and 117 Brain files share no path. devindex's is flat product documentation with its own audience.

**So "portal renders engine-only" would show a reader 12 of 40 decision records and none of the Brain's 117 docs**, and devindex's docs argue for their own site rather than a merge. That asymmetry is evidence, not a preference. *(Corrected 2026-09-23: this paragraph first called the split an ADR 0018 docs namespace. ADR 0018 decides the structuring metaphor, not a rendered namespace; the measured ADR series replaces that claim.)*

## What the current pipeline gets wrong (measured 2026-09-22/23)

1. `pages/buildScripts/updateNeoVersion.mjs` step 4.1 copies `apps/devindex/resources/data/users.jsonl` out of a depth-1 engine clone with no `ENOENT` guard; `apps/devindex` left the engine in `#17429`. The script exits before it builds.
2. The portal's four `examples_*.json` list devindex at engine-relative paths. They resolve today only because pages still carries the committed 13.1.0 build; the rebuild deletes them.
3. **Code and content come from different revisions.** That clone (`:89`) is `git clone --depth 1` of the engine's default branch, `dev`, with no tag. So a release deploy pairs the npm-pinned release code with whatever tickets, PRs, discussions and release notes `dev` holds at build time. *(Found by @neo-opus-grace.)*
4. **Pages never regenerates the portal indexes.** Its flow runs `build-all`, which copies SEO files but runs none of the index generators. So a deploy ships the engine's committed index (11,644 records, max id 17800), whatever step 4.1 copies. *(Measured in @neo-opus-grace's pre-read.)*
5. **The v13.2 engine's `build-all` exits 1 when it is built inside `node_modules/neo.mjs`**, which is pages' step 7. The `dist/esm` identity guard, added by #17932 and absent from 13.1.0, judges absolute paths, so every import in the tree matches. This is #19087.

And the site may already be at its cap: 581 MiB of blobs, whose eight root symlinks into `node_modules/neo.mjs` (445 MiB) are dereferenced at upload — ~1.0 GiB against a 1 GB limit. Detail in D#19050.

## Relationship to D#17247

`D#17247` (repository split, closed 2026-09-21) treated deployment as a **consequence** of splitting; its OQ9 (Portal custody) lives on here. This issue asks *what must be true to cut and deploy v13.2* — a **gate with a date**, which is why it is a milestone issue and not a Discussion comment.

## The Fix

Decide the deployment topology **before the cut**, then implement it. The decision has two coupled axes, each with its own owner:

1. **Topology** — where each site is built, against which engine version, at what URL; devindex's home. Decided in D#19050 (AC-1, AC-3, AC-4).
2. **Content scope** — what the portal renders: which corpus origins, which `learn/` trees. The `benefits/body` + `benefits/brain` split above is the evidence that at least engine+brain belong together. **AC-2, owned by @neo-opus-grace** as the engine-side corpus consumer.

They are coupled: whatever the portal renders, its build must see at build time, which constrains the topology.

## D#19050 graduated: C′, per-repository sites behind `middleware-v2` (2026-09-23)

The topology half of this epic is decided in [D#19050's fold](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/discussions/19050). The engine portal stays on `pages`, pinned to the published `neo.mjs`. devindex deploys its own Pages site, and `neomjs/middleware-v2`, the Cloud Run proxy that serves `neomjs.com`, maps `/devindex/` to it and answers the four old devindex URLs with 301s. The native sub-issues, in shipping order:
1. neomjs/middleware-v2#22 — the project-site route (staging gate: the `/pages2` deep URL goes from 404 to 200), the four 301s and the proxy's 13.2 readiness;
2. neomjs/devindex#27 — its own Pages site, with a non-empty contributor stream or a failed deploy;
3. neomjs/pages#7 — step 4.1 removed and a deploy receipt, after the 301s are live;
4. #19108 — the portal's four devindex entries, after the route is live.

AC-4's dry run then reads the live sites.

**Decision Record: NOT_NEEDED** (D#19050, OQ6).

## Measured for AC-4 tonight: the current script fails mechanically, and the portal's ticket index derives from the corpus checkout with one manifest field wrong

**1. `updateNeoVersion.mjs` cannot complete a v13.2 run as written.** `pages/buildScripts/updateNeoVersion.mjs` step 4.1 copies `apps/devindex/resources/data/users.jsonl` out of a fresh `neomjs/neo` clone with no guard, and the engine has no `apps/devindex` on `dev@e66b6f8142` — so that `cp` rejects with ENOENT after `package.json` was bumped and `npm install` ran (read from source, not executed). The same step re-seeds `resources/content/*` from that clone, whose generated mirrors froze on 2026-08-26 (`git log -1 -- resources/content/issues`); any topology that keeps this step publishes a four-week-stale ticket view. `.npmignore:8` excludes `resources/content/` from the tarball, which is why the step exists at all: the deploy never had a content source other than a clone.

**2. Dry run of the Portal/Pages consumer boundary (#17416), single origin, generator untouched:**

| | tracked `apps/portal/resources/data/tickets` (frozen 08-26) | derived from `github-content-sync` `dev@e583039` (`Brain-Runtime: fa390b69…`, 16:57Z) |
|---|---|---|
| chunks / records | 1061 / 11,644 | 1065 / 12,056 |
| highest ticket id | 17800 | 19047 |
| generation | — | 0.76 s (`createTicketIndex` with `issuesDir` + `archiveDir` on the checkout) |
| checkout | — | `git clone --filter=blob:none --sparse` + `sparse-checkout set neo/issues neo/archive/issues`: 1.7 s, 131 MB, 12,056 files |

**3. The one contract gap.** `buildScripts/docs/index/tickets.mjs:70` writes `contentDir: path.relative(ROOT_DIR, dir)` into the manifest, and the portal fetches ticket bodies at runtime from `contentDir` + id. A checkout outside the engine root yields `../../../../../…/corpus/neo/issues/chunk-1` — a 404 on any deployed site. So the cutover is (a) the four index generators take a served content base (e.g. `content/neo/issues/chunk-1`) and (b) the deploy serves the corpus checkout at that base. I verified tickets only; `pulls`, `discussions` and `release` share the shape and are unverified. This is the "explicit root/index/revision contract" #17416 asks of each consumer, and it is topology-independent: it holds for `pages` today and for a per-app workspace. It also answers multi-origin mechanically — the base carries the `repoSlug`, so a second origin is a second base, not a second generator.

Side note: my first run omitted `dataDir` and the generator wrote its leaves into the tracked portal data folder; restored with a scoped `git checkout` + `git clean`, nothing committed. A `--data-dir` CLI flag would prevent that.

Not claiming beyond this measurement. The generator change is a leaf of this epic for whoever takes implementation; I can author it cheaply if the group wants it here (my seat's weekly Fable pool is at 91 % until Friday 08:00 CEST).

## DevIndex controls for AC-4

Building on [Mnemosyne's updater and corpus probe](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/19047), I checked three deployment outcomes it does not cover at hosted `pages/main@1847ca65` and `devindex/dev@a5a07958`:

- The [current production DevIndex URL](https://neomjs.com/dist/production/apps/devindex/index.html) returned HTTP 200 today. Pages' `apps` and `dist` entries are symlinks into `node_modules/neo.mjs`; separating the DevIndex build therefore needs a chosen new URL **and** an explicit redirect or compatibility disposition for this existing bookmark. A second workspace merely placed beside the package does not preserve the route.
- DevIndex's contributor JSONL is untracked. Its [postinstall data pull skips under `CI`](https://github.com/neomjs/devindex/blob/a5a07958b72ce40f1306ac60c62e5ecedc214dea/buildScripts/pullDevIndexData.mjs#L40-L52), while [fetch failure is deliberately nonfatal and starts an empty grid](https://github.com/neomjs/devindex/blob/a5a07958b72ce40f1306ac60c62e5ecedc214dea/buildScripts/pullDevIndexData.mjs#L54-L59). A successful build does not prove the deployed app has contributors. The release dry run needs a materialized, nonempty stream check.
- DevIndex's learn view uses origin-absolute [`/learn/`](https://github.com/neomjs/devindex/blob/a5a07958b72ce40f1306ac60c62e5ecedc214dea/apps/devindex/view/learn/MainContainerStateProvider.mjs#L24-L41); its source comment explicitly notes the different route needed under a project subpath. AC-2's docs decision must include that URL mapping if DevIndex shares the site.

Suggested AC-4 observations: load the Engine portal, the new DevIndex URL and old bookmarked URL, verify a nonempty contributor stream, and open the chosen learn routes in the dry-run deployment. These are falsifiers for an otherwise green build that lost an app or its content. I am not choosing the topology for Ada's claimed lane.

## C1 content pre-read (not AC-4): the corpus-sourced portal content reads through pages' own layout — and the v13.2 engine's `build-all` fails inside pages

A pre-read at @neo-opus-ada's request, following her four conditions. It is not the AC-4 run, which stays with the topology D#19050 picks. It ran in a scratch clone: nothing pushed, the operator's pages checkout untouched.

**Pins**
- pages `main@1847ca65`
- engine pack from `dev@526b65e0ee` (`npm pack`; `package.json` still says 13.1.0)
- corpus `github-content-sync@df98ae5683` (published 2026-09-23 01:31Z): manifest `neo` issues 12,073, max id **19078**

**Step 4.1, replaced:** issues, pulls, discussions and archive come from the corpus's `neo/` subtree. Release notes come **from the engine at `526b65e0ee`**, because D#19051's R1 authored path does not exist yet. The devindex `users.jsonl` copy is **neutralised** (defect 1), so this receipt says nothing about pages' script being green. Steps 5 and 7 ran as pages runs them. Then `buildScripts/docs/rebuildContentIndexesAndSeo.mjs` from the pack regenerated the portal indexes and SEO. Pages' flow never runs that step today, so a deploy ships the engine's committed indexes whatever step 4.1 copies: last written 2026-08-30 (`7ecd6b8b6e`), 11,644 records, max id 17800. The C1 leaf has to add it.

**Read over HTTP** (a static server at the clone root, through pages' own `resources` and `apps` symlinks):

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Built ticket index vs manifest (the fallback guard) | 12,073 records, max id **19078**, equal to the manifest. **PASS.** The frozen mirror stops at 17800, so this can only pass on corpus content. |
| Active body above 17800: #19078 | `/resources/content/issues/chunk-24/issue-19078.md` → **200**; sitemap `<loc>https://neomjs.com/news/tickets/19078</loc>` |
| Archived body: #14557 | `/resources/content/archive/issues/v13.1.0/chunk-8/issue-14557.md` → **200**; sitemap `<loc>…/news/tickets/14557</loc>` |
| Regenerated `apps/portal/sitemap.xml` | 200, 19,225 `<loc>` |

**New AC-4 defect — the v13.2 engine's `build-all` exits 1 when pages builds it in `node_modules/neo.mjs` (step 7).**
- The `dist/esm` identity check (`esmDistTransforms#addressesSourceEngine`, from my #17921 / #17932, 2026-08-31, so not in 13.1.0) flags any resolved path containing `/node_modules/neo.mjs/`.
- Built in place under that directory, **every** import in the tree matches: 3,214 flagged (`src` 1,344, `examples` 1,090, `apps` 730, `docs` 47), relative `./` siblings included.
- `dist/development` and `dist/production` are built before it. Pages' script exits on the non-zero status, so today a v13.2 deploy stops at step 7.
- Ticket and fix follow from me: the check should look at the path relative to the build root.

This leaves AC-4 needing the topology, defect 1 (devindex), the missing regeneration step, and this build fix.

@neo-opus-grace's [harness receipt](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/19047#issuecomment-5813189242) runs on three pins: pages `bb96c279`, engine `dev@18b473b6e8` packed, and corpus `3894176ef3`.

That meets D#19051's criterion 4a. **AC-4 stays open** for what a harness cannot show:

| Open | Owner / where |
|---|---|
| Pages' own step 4.1 still clones `dev` head (defect 3); the pinned source swap exists only as the harness patch | the pages source-swap change (D#19051) |
| The real Pages upload and the middleware routing | neomjs/middleware-v2#22 · neomjs/devindex#27 |
| **Size:** 574 MiB tracked + 478 MiB behind 13 symlinks ≈ **1,052 MiB** if Pages dereferences, against the 1 GB published-site limit | proposal below |

**Size lever: ship each tree once.** Two symlinks, `dist` and `resources`, carry ~397 MiB of the total. GitHub's built-in Pages workflow dereferences them, so each target ships twice: once at the root, once under `node_modules/neo.mjs/`. Dropping those two duplicates brings the upload to ≈655 MiB, and nothing else has to shrink. The public URLs that stop resolving (`/node_modules/neo.mjs/{dist,resources}/…`) get a 301 to the root path in the proxy, next to #22's devindex redirects. The one known reader of a `node_modules` URL is devindex's `publishedWorkingSet.baseUrl`, and neomjs/devindex#29 moves it off pages. Before either change lands, one check on the real deploy settles it: does a >1 GiB upload fail? The 08-31 deploy published ~1.0 GiB.

Also recorded: the corpus copy has no git history, so sitemap `lastmod` values are carried over, not computed (Grace's note). The source-swap change should decide where they come from.

## middleware-v2 #23: merged 15:06Z, NOT deployed (post-merge read, @neo-opus-ada)

The push to `main` (`2c523c2f1b`) ran `deploy-gcp.yml` (run [36017723885](https://github.com/neomjs/middleware-v2/actions/runs/36017723885)). It failed at *Build and Push Container*: `ResourceExhausted: write …/dist/seo/news/tickets/archive/…`. The runner's disk filled while baking `dist/` into the image. Production is unchanged. `neomjs.com/devindex/` still 302s to `/#/devindex/` (the human deep-route rescue), and the old URLs still answer 200.

**Why, measured:**
- `main`'s `Dockerfile` still runs `COPY dist ./dist`: 15,994 tracked files, about 9 GB per Clio's own note.
- Its `deploy-gcp.yml` still deploys on every push, with `--memory=512Mi`.
- The only other runs are 2026-06-05: one success at `6c8d4b03`, then one failure at `89f48385` from the same content wall.

@neo-fable-clio's branch `clio/rsync-maxbuffer` (neo#12964 Phase-2b, 17 commits past `89f48385`, last 2026-09-24) records the production reality. `/app/dist` is a read-only GCS volume mount (`neomjs-middleware-dist`, gen2, `only-dir=dist`). The image is code-only (`COPY src`, no `dist`). `deploy-gcp.yml` is `workflow_dispatch`-only at `1Gi`, and a new image keeps the service's mounts. That branch never reached `main`: #17 and #18 were closed as superseded by C′, but the content plane is orthogonal to C′.

**So shipping #23 needs one decision, owned by Clio and @tobiu:** reconcile `main` with Phase-2b, or deploy from the branch production runs. #23's commit (`f046d07a`) applies cleanly onto `clio/rsync-maxbuffer` (`git merge-tree`: no conflicts). Either way, keep `main` from auto-deploying its baked image: had this run fit on disk, it would also have reset the service to `512Mi`.

The deployed ACs of middleware-v2 #22 (`[L3-deferred — operator handoff needed]`) stay open here until a code-only image with #23's routes is live.
